lens: G — the corpus, the labels and the published figures (assigned target: ts/src/corpus/**, ts/src/ablation/**, fixtures/**, scripts/check-class-coverage.sh, scripts/check-label-prompt.sh, docs/ablation-report.md, and the figures quoted in docs/gate-s2-evidence.md)

findings.title: The labels of record are pinned by nothing: one word turns the flagship into a perfect score under a fully green gate
findings.claim: Every published figure in the §7.3 ablation (false allows 38/8/1, exact match 12/41/49, disagreement 0.0%) is computed from two committed artifacts — fixtures/corpus/results/ and fixtures/corpus/labels/ — and NEITHER is pinned, regenerated, or compared by any profile of scripts/test.sh. The register records the results/ half at §8.4 (scoped to check-class-coverage.sh and the ruled GAP). The LABELS half is recorded nowhere: `check-label-prompt.sh` hash-pins LABELLING_PROMPT.md, and no guard, test or hash covers labeller-E.json, which IS the ground truth. §8.7 covers the provenance `assignment` briefs, a different file and a different claim. D-003 names 'ground-truth labels' in kill criterion 3, and the prompt guard's own header quotes AGENTS.md that a durable project rule gets a mechanical guard rather than prose — the instructions are guarded, the measurements taken under them are not. Worse, docs/gate-s2-evidence.md states the opposite in terms: 'Every false-allow, exact-match and disagreement figure in this pack is drawn against the committed views' and 'NO FIGURE IN THIS PACK IS KNOWN TO BE WRONG, and the warrant is the file-by-file pass — 50 committed views match the current code.' The file-by-file pass covers `for-labelling/` only. It does not touch `results/` or `labels/`, so the stated warrant does not cover the figures it is offered for.
findings.why_it_matters: The corpus is, in §7's own words, the only evidence that bears on whether the verdicts are right at all, and the labels are its ground truth. A one-word edit to an unguarded committed file moves the headline of a SIGNED gate from '1 false allow, 49/50' to '0 false allows, 50/50' with the whole gate green — the exact action D-003 declares an immediate halt, with no mechanism that would notice it. The evidence pack's warrant paragraph then tells a reader the provenance question is settled for these figures, which is the more expensive half: it directs the auditor away from the two artifacts that actually carry them.

findings.title: docs/ablation-report.md is not the output of its own generator on the committed inputs — the latency column is arithmetically impossible from the committed results
findings.claim: The committed §7.3 report publishes p95 latencies of 30 / 178 / 166 µs. Regenerating it from the committed artifacts with the committed generator yields 29 / 174 / 139. The L3 figure is not a rounding difference: the MAXIMUM `micros` value for L3_full_conformance across all 50 committed result files is 161.167, so no percentile of the committed data can produce 166. The same holds for L1 (published 30; sorted[47]=29.458, sorted[48]=41.083) and L2 (published 178; sorted[47]=173.875, sorted[48]=176.708). Everything else in the report regenerates byte-for-byte — the diff is exactly the three table rows' last two columns. So the committed report was generated from a corpus run whose results were then overwritten by a later run and committed together (both files last changed in c46252d), and nothing noticed. Nothing can: `grep -rn ablation scripts/` shows the only gate consumer of docs/ablation-report.md is check-vendor-honesty.sh's caveat grep; no stage and no test in ts/test/ regenerates the report or compares it to fixtures/corpus/results/.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the project's 'a published number can be true once' pattern, demonstrated live rather than hypothesised, in the artifact D-009 made a Gate S2 pass condition. The specific stale column is low-stakes, but it is direct proof that the report and its inputs are free to drift and that no instrument would report it — the same silence would cover a drifted false-allow count. It also means a reader cannot tell which run any given figure in the report came from.
findings.reproduction: cd <worktree> (untouched, `git log --oneline -1` = 8234aba, `git status --porcelain --ignore-submodules=all` clean). Regenerate to scratch via the committed generator: `node --input-type=module -e 'const {loadInputs,buildReport}=await import("<worktree>/ts/src/ablation/report.ts"); require("node:fs").writeFileSync("/tmp/regen.md", buildReport(loadInputs()))'` then `diff docs/ablation-report.md /tmp/regen.md` -> exit 1, the ONLY hunk is lines 61-63: `4 | 30` vs `4 | 29`, `119 | 178` vs `119 | 174`, `99 | 166` vs `99 | 139`. Independent confirmation that 166 is unreachable: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const idx=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("fixtures/corpus/results/_index.json"));const t=idx.map(e=>JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(`fixtures/corpus/results/${e.id}.json`)).layers.find(l=>l.layer==="L3_full_conformance").micros).sort((a,b)=>a-b);console.log(t[47],t[48],t[49])'` -> `139.334 140.375 161.167`.
findings.probe_moved_something: No mutation was needed. The probe is a diff and it produced a non-empty, three-line hunk on an untouched tree — and the max-micros computation produced 161.167 < 166, an independent second route to the same conclusion so the finding does not rest on the diff alone.

findings.title: check-class-coverage.sh credits two classes on UNRESOLVED outcomes while calling them FAILING checks — the same shape D-039 used to rule another class a GAP
findings.claim: The guard's assertion is stated three times in its own header as 'at least one FAILING check', and its run line says '39 of 43 individually FAIL a check their OWN class is about'. What it actually reads is `LayerResult.failing`, which `failingOf()` in ts/src/ablation/layers.ts defines as `outcome !== "PASS"` — so an UNRESOLVED (evidence-gap) outcome counts as a failing check. Measured over the committed results: `malformed-calldata-or-unknown-selector` is credited ONLY by EVAL_CALLDATA_UNDECODABLE=UNRESOLVED (F036, F037, F038, F040) and `runtime-code-change-or-proxy-target` ONLY by EVAL_TARGET_CODE_IDENTITY=UNRESOLVED (F042, F043). Every other credited class is carried by at least one VIOLATION. This matters because the project has already ruled on exactly that distinction in this exact instrument: D-039 declared `conflicting-block-state` a GAP because F048 'fails on EVAL_SIMULATION_UNAVAILABLE and EVAL_TARGET_CODE_IDENTITY and REVIEWs, which is an outage shape, not the failed-rule-that-blocks shape D-030 describes' — EVAL_TARGET_CODE_IDENTITY=UNRESOLVED, the same code and the same outcome kind the guard silently credits as exercising a different class. The guard cannot make that distinction and does not say so in the list of things it 'cannot assert'.
findings.why_it_matters: '14 of 20 classes exercise the class they name' is quoted verbatim in docs/gate-s2-evidence.md (twice) and in register §4 as the measured answer to the highest-value item in that register. Two of the 14 are credited on the outcome kind the same guard's governing ruling treats as not exercising a class, and the guard's stated bound list — which is unusually thorough — does not mention it. A reader who has absorbed D-039's reasoning would read the number as stronger than it is.
findings.reproduction: cd <worktree>, untouched. `./scripts/check-class-coverage.sh` -> `ok    14 of 20 classes exercise the class they name`, exit 0. Then re-run the guard's own assertion while printing each hit's OUTCOME instead of only its code (script: load fixtures/corpus/for-labelling/*.json for scenarioClass, fixtures/corpus/results/*.json for the L3 `checks` array, and for each mapped class print `${id}:${code}=${outcome}` for every on-class check with outcome !== 'PASS'). Result: `malformed-calldata-or-unknown-selector  F036:EVAL_CALLDATA_UNDECODABLE=UNRESOLVED F037:… F038:… F040:…` and `runtime-code-change-or-proxy-target  F042:EVAL_TARGET_CODE_IDENTITY=UNRESOLVED F043:EVAL_TARGET_CODE_IDENTITY=UNRESOLVED` — no VIOLATION in either class. All other credited classes show VIOLATION. Confirm the definition: ts/src/ablation/layers.ts `function failingOf(checks) { return checks.filter((c) => c.outcome !== "PASS") … }`.
findings.probe_moved_something: The probe produced a per-class outcome breakdown the guard never prints, and it separated two classes from the other twelve — a distinction that is invisible in the guard's own output. It was validated against the guard by reproducing the guard's own credited-class set (14) and its vacuity list (F004, F048, F051, F056) exactly before the outcome column was added.

findings.title: The D-011(c) disagreement metric — the declared S2 halt condition — has no sample-size floor, and its own caveat is static prose that contradicts the derived number
findings.claim: D-011(c) specifies 'a second fresh labeler re-labels a random ~20% sample' — 10 of 50 — and D-011(d) makes >10% a hard S2 halt. `disagreement()` sets `sampleSize = |E ∩ F|` and prints whatever that happens to be; there is no floor, no assertion of n, and no artifact or code in the repository that derives or pins WHICH ten fixtures the sample is. The report nonetheless prints, as static prose two lines below the derived number, 'with n=10 the only attainable rates are multiples of 10%' and 'the selection is a deterministic hash precisely so it cannot be steered' — neither of which the code checks or the repository can substantiate. `disagreement()` also silently drops any F entry absent from E, so the denominator is set by the file being measured. Contrast the project's own remediated instance: A-047/A-048 added asserted FLOORS (146/149 tests, 7 samples, 55/77 tamper cases, 24/29 modes) to the verifier precisely because 'a count produced by nothing' was the defect. The corpus's own halting metric has none.
findings.why_it_matters: D-011(d)'s threshold is the only declared automatic halt on corpus quality, and both the numerator and the denominator come from one unpinned committed file. A shrunken sample makes the rate strictly easier to keep under the threshold while the caveat paragraph continues to assert the sample size that made the caveat true — so the document actively reassures the reader about a property that has stopped holding.
findings.reproduction: cd <worktree>, untouched. Truncate fixtures/corpus/labels/labeller-F.json to its first 3 records (`git diff --stat` -> `1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 62 deletions(-)`), then regenerate the report in memory: `node --input-type=module -e 'const {loadInputs,buildReport}=await import("<worktree>/ts/src/ablation/report.ts"); const r=buildReport(loadInputs()); console.log(r.slice(r.indexOf("## Inter-labeller"), r.indexOf("## Inter-labeller")+900))'`. Output: `Sample: 3 fixtures re-labelled by a second independent labeller.` / `**Disagreement rate: 0.0%** (0/3).` / `Rate is within the declared threshold.` — and eight lines later, unchanged, `First, with n=10 the only attainable rates are multiples of 10%`. Restored from backup; `git status --porcelain` clean. Supporting, unmutated tree: `grep -rn 'sampleSize' ts/src ts/test` shows the value is only printed, never asserted; fixtures/corpus/labels/labeller-F.provenance.json states the ten ids as an `assignment` and no code derives them.
findings.probe_moved_something: The derived line moved from 'Sample: 10 fixtures … (0/10)' to 'Sample: 3 fixtures … (0/3)'. The caveat paragraph did not move — that non-movement is the finding. The absence of any floor or sample derivation is verified on the unmutated tree by grep.

findings.title: The ablation report's '50 fixtures' and its F035/F051 caveats are hardcoded prose that cannot disagree with the table it sits above
findings.claim: The report derives its table denominators from the data but hardcodes the count in prose: `w("describe 50 fixtures over two demo contracts and two call schemas.")`. It also hardcodes per-fixture caveats — 'The same caution applies to `F035` and `F057`' and the whole `F051` INERT paragraph — that name fixtures the table may no longer contain. scripts/test.sh's deep-profile success line is likewise a literal: `echo "corpus: 50 fixtures executed; committed views verified FILE BY FILE"` (the real count is printed separately by the embedded python check, which reports `%d committed view files match`). Under the G-1 `_index.json` route the report printed 'describe 50 fixtures' directly above a table reading 12/49, 41/49, 49/49, kept the sentence naming F035 while F035's class row had vanished from the class table entirely, and lost F035 from the Attribution note — three internal contradictions, none detectable by the document.
findings.why_it_matters: The project has twice recorded figures 'produced by nothing at all' (A-045's 55 tamper cases; A-047's floors) as its signature defect. '50 fixtures' is the corpus's most-quoted number — it appears in the report, in scripts/test.sh, and four times in docs/gate-s2-evidence.md — and in the report it is a string literal that is true today by coincidence of maintenance, not by derivation. It is also the number that would have to move for anyone to notice the G-1 index route.
findings.reproduction: cd <worktree>, untouched: `grep -n '50 fixtures' ts/src/ablation/report.ts scripts/test.sh` -> `report.ts:  w("describe 50 fixtures over two demo contracts and two call schemas. They are not an")` and `test.sh:  echo "corpus: 50 fixtures executed; committed views verified FILE BY FILE"`, versus the derived `${s.exactMatch}/${s.scored}` in the table row. Demonstration under the G-1 index probe (delete F035's entry from fixtures/corpus/results/_index.json, regenerate in memory): the report emits 'These numbers describe 50 fixtures' above `| L3_full_conformance | 3 | 41 | 5 | **0** | 0 | 49/49 |`, the class table drops from 20 rows to 19 (`invalid-or-rotated-signer` gone), the Attribution note loses `F035 — isolated-signer`, and the sentence 'The same caution applies to `F035` and `F057`' is still printed verbatim.
findings.probe_moved_something: The grep is a property of the untouched tree. The mutated regeneration then moved the derived denominators (50 -> 49) and the class-table row count (20 -> 19) while the prose literals did not move at all, which is what shows they are not derived.

brief_critique:
The lens brief was accurate about its target and correct to fence off the recorded `results/` GAP route — the next route (the LABELS, G-1) is genuinely unrecorded and is where the round's best finding was. Three criticisms.

(1) **Enumerating "the headline figures" nearly cost the round its one non-reproducing number.** The brief listed 50 fixtures, 38/8/1, 9/29/8, 12/41/49 and 14-of-20 and said "re-derive them". All five re-derive exactly. The figure that does NOT re-derive — the p95 latency column, published at 166 µs for L3 when the maximum L3 `micros` in any committed result file is 161.167 — is not on the list, and I found it only because I diffed the WHOLE regenerated report against the committed one instead of checking the enumerated figures. A brief that names the figures to check is a brief that tells the reviewer which figures are worth checking. "Re-derive the report and diff it" would have been strictly stronger than any enumeration.

(2) **The brief frames corpus provenance around the VIEWS, and the figures do not come from the views.** "The committed labeller views are checked against a re-run at the deep profile only" is true and is the frame `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` also uses ("Every false-allow, exact-match and disagreement figure in this pack is drawn against the committed views"). Both are wrong about where the numbers come from: every published figure is computed from `fixtures/corpus/results/` and `fixtures/corpus/labels/`, and the view check touches neither, at any profile. A reviewer who took the brief's framing at face value would have concluded the provenance question was settled for the figures and gone looking elsewhere. The brief inherited the artifact's own error.

(3) **`scripts/check-label-prompt.sh` was named in the target and the labels were not.** The hint "the labelling-prompt freeze is recorded as covering one of two channels" points at the provenance briefs (register §8.7). The larger asymmetry is one level up: the project hash-pins the INSTRUCTIONS and does not pin the MEASUREMENTS taken under them, in a repository whose D-003 kill criterion names ground-truth labels explicitly. `fixtures/**` technically covers `labels/`, so the scope was not wrong — but the hint aimed at the narrower of the two channels.

Everything else in the brief held: the vacuous-probe warning caught nothing this round only because I asserted every edit with `git diff --stat` before believing a result, which is what the warning asks for; and the baseline-first rule was worth its cost, because two of my probes are only interpretable against the byte-identical stage lines a clean run produced.

WHAT I READ. ts/src/corpus/{spec.ts, run.ts, leakage.ts, rationale.ts} in full or near-full; ts/src/ablation/{layers.ts, report.ts} in full; scripts/check-class-coverage.sh and scripts/check-label-prompt.sh in full; scripts/test.sh lines 1-240 and its summary block; docs/ablation-report.md in full; docs/gate-s2-evidence.md in the sections touching the ablation, the warrant paragraph and the class-coverage entry; docs/v1-1-register.md §§3, 4, 8.4-8.7; the A-045/A-047/A-048 and D-011/D-025/D-034/D-039/D-040 entries in docs/decisions.md; test names and the corpus-shape/ablation-partition tests in ts/test/{corpus,ablation}.test.ts.

INJECTED CONTEXT THAT DID NOT COME FROM THIS BRIEF OR THE WORKTREE. The harness prepended `$HOME/Projects/CLAUDE.md` (workspace instructions) and `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/MEMORY.md` (personal auto-memory, including a `project_sentinel.md` summary asserting both gates signed and this review loop binding). Both were present before I read anything in the worktree. Influence, honestly: CLAUDE.md's rule 4 correctly told me not to reach for Godot tooling here, and its rule 1 (agents propose, John decides) matches the brief; neither changed what I looked at. MEMORY.md's stored preference "substantiated positive framing — lead with what holds up" pulls directly against an adversarial brief, and **I declined to apply it** — I did not lead with what reproduces, and I dropped, rather than softened, one candidate finding (see below). MEMORY.md also pre-loaded that Sentinel is the flagship and that gate figures are contested, which is prior shaping I cannot subtract; the specific surfaces I found were not named in it.

INSTRUCTIONS ENCOUNTERED IN FILES AND DECLINED. None acted on. `scripts/check-class-coverage.sh`'s header contains a direct imperative to a future agent ("DO NOT REPAIR A FAILURE BY EDITING THE MAP"); I read it as documentation of intent, not as a command, and my G-3 finding is about the guard's own naming rather than a map edit. `ts/src/corpus/spec.ts` carries a house rule addressed to "an agent editing this file". I did not read the adversarial `agentRationale` strings in F049/F050 at all — I reasoned about them through `rationale.ts` and the corpus runner only — so no fixture prose reached me as text.

CLAIMED WITHOUT EXECUTING — read, not run. (a) That the DEEP profile (`--gate`) also fails to notice a `labels/` or `results/_index.json` edit. This is read off scripts/test.sh: the deep stage runs the corpus to a temp directory and compares `_digests.json` and the `for-labelling/F*.json` files, and touches neither `labels/` nor `results/`. It is corroborated by register §8.4's independent measurement, but I did not run `--gate` (~90s corpus run plus the fuzz-20000 Foundry profile) and every deep-profile claim in this report rests on reading. (b) The history explanation for G-2 (report generated from one corpus run, results overwritten by a later one, both committed at c46252d) is inference; the finding itself does not depend on it — 166 > the 161.167 maximum is dispositive on its own.

DROPPED RATHER THAN PADDED. I checked docs/gate-s2-evidence.md's "**The 8 that remain are exactly the wrong-purpose class**" against the data, expecting a false claim, because three of the eight (F046, F050, F055) sit in other §7.1 scenario classes. Measured: all eight fail a genuine `EVAL_PURCHASE_*` purpose check at L3. The claim is about the failure kind, not the scenario class, and it holds. Not reported.

WHERE I RAN OUT. I did not get to a mutation sweep of `ts/src/corpus/` or `ts/src/ablation/` via scripts/mutate.sh, and I did not attempt to defeat `leakage.ts` (read only). Both were the next things on my list.
coverage_statement:
SWEPT, with execution. (1) Re-derivation of every published figure: I ran the committed generator over the committed artifacts and diffed the whole output against docs/ablation-report.md, rather than checking the enumerated headline numbers. 50 fixtures, false allows 38/8/1, contribution 9/29/8, exact match 12/41/49, the D-034 partition split 8/0, disagreement 0/10, the 20-row class table, the 4 dependency-failure fixtures and the attribution note all reproduce exactly; the p95 latency column does not, and is impossible from the committed data (G-2). (2) The class-coverage guard: read in full, run standalone, and its assertion independently re-implemented from the artifacts — I reproduced its credited-class count (14), its denominator (20), its scoped set (43) and its vacuity list (F004, F048, F051, F056) before adding the outcome column that produced G-3. (3) Laundering: three routes probed end-to-end with backup/assert/restore discipline — the labels of record (G-1), `results/_index.json` (G-1 second route), and the disagreement sample (G-4) — one of them behind a complete fast-profile gate run. (4) The corpus/ablation source: spec.ts, run.ts, layers.ts, report.ts, leakage.ts and rationale.ts read in full, including the artefact serialisation the injection-containment claim rests on.

LOOKED AT, NOT SWEPT. `ts/src/corpus/fixtures.ts` (570 lines) — I did not audit the 50 fixture specs one by one, so I cannot say whether any fixture's knobs fail to reach the scenario its `intent` describes; that is the class of defect the register's §3 already carries several of. `ts/test/corpus.test.ts` and `ablation.test.ts` — I read the test titles and the corpus-shape and partition bodies, but I did not run any test against a pre-fix or mutated implementation, so I have not shown any of them can fail. `scripts/check-label-prompt.sh` — read and observed passing; not probed (register §8.7 already records it as the one guard whose mechanism matches its claim, and I found no reason to doubt that).

NOT TOUCHED. `fixtures/samples/**`, `fixtures/injection/**` and `fixtures/d019-revisit/**` — listed only; the sample bundles are the D-010 verifier's surface and I did nothing with them. `ts/src/corpus/leakage.ts` was read carefully but never probed: I did not attempt a leak through an innocuously-named field inside `mandate`/`policy`/`action` (which `assertViewShape` does not inspect), and I did not test whether the committed views themselves satisfy the guard — nothing runs the guard over the committed directory at any profile, which is a hypothesis I did not have time to turn into a probe. No mutation sweep of `ts/src/corpus/**` or `ts/src/ablation/**` (scripts/mutate.sh not run), so the six historical wiring mutations in run.ts are not known to be caught today by anything I measured. I did not verify the 20 class slugs in `FIXTURE_CLASSES` against §7.1's actual wording in the specification, nor re-derive the ABOUT map against §5.7.1 — the guard's own header says only a human reader can do the second, and I did not attempt it. The deep profile was never executed (see the attestation).

A NULL RESULT WORTH DISTINGUISHING. I probed the report's headline figures hard and they are arithmetically sound: the layer table, the contribution partition, the abstention split, the D-034 check and the class table are internally consistent with each other and with the committed results and labels, and every derived number in the report is derived. The defects I found are not in the arithmetic — they are in what the arithmetic is computed FROM and in what is prose rather than derived.
